props.command: Week 6 of the Medhavy physics engine: we built a benchmark harness — what did it say?

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Jash Shah, and this video is based on week six of the Medhavy physics engine — benchmark week, and the most honest number we have.

props.sparkLine: No wrong answers. Not enough answers
props.title: The benchmark result

beats.narration_text: We built a benchmark harness against U.G. Physics, from I.C.M.L. twenty twenty-five. The engine gave zero wrong answers — and almost zero right ones. That sounds like a failure. It's actually the system telling the truth.

props.sparkLine: The gap is coverage, not correctness
props.title: Why: the scope gap

data.label: of UGPhysics asks for symbolic derivations
data.note: Those sit outside the 31-card formula library's scope.

beats.narration_text: About sixty percent of U.G. Physics asks for symbolic derivations — work outside the thirty-one card library. Remember week three: no card, no guess. So it doesn't answer wrong. It doesn't answer.

beats.narration_text: Week six in one line: when the engine answers, it's right — the gap is how often it can.

props.command: My system scored zero wrong answers and almost zero right answers on a benchmark. Explain the three most likely reasons, and what each one says about whether the system actually works.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Ask Claude how a system can score zero wrong and almost zero right at the same time. The answer changes how you read every benchmark.
Physics engine, week six. Always undisputed.
